BeforeSideTurnEnd.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The arithmetic, the empty-hand guard and the Unpowered prop all match, and the slot is correctly ahead of the hand flush -- but the sim has no sub-phase ordering inside its turn-end walk (G1) and no AutoPostPlay phase before it (G2), so the hand this relic counts can differ from the hand the game counts.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly / Early / plain sub-phases are flattened into one listener walk, and Cloak Clasp is the named witness
guards.issue: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guard G12 owns this mechanism and verdicts it a gap; binding rule 3 means it is cited and matched, not re-derived. C# guarantees ordering by running three complete passes -- BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly, then BeforeSideTurnEndEarly, then BeforeSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1238-1261) -- and CloakClasp.cs:24 sits in the LAST of the three. The sim's hooks.on_player_turn_end (hooks.py:297-301) is a single `for l in list(self._listeners)` pass, so the guaranteed position becomes registration order. The seam's executed evidence is this relic's: with a 5-card hand, '[cloak_clasp, orichalcum] gives 5 block and [orichalcum, cloak_clasp] gives 11; C# always gives 11 because the VeryEarly snapshot runs before ANY plain listener'. Both sides ported -- Orichalcum is an Uncommon relic whose C# implementation is deliberately two-phase (Orichalcum.cs:44-56 snapshots `Block > 0` in VeryEarly), Fake Orichalcum and Ripple Basin are the same shape, and Cloak Clasp is Rare in the transcribed grab bag (confirmed by `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3-pool`). Pinned there by test_orichalcum_snapshots_block_before_other_turn_end_listeners.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the AutoPostPlay phase does not exist, so end-of-turn auto-plays that C# runs BEFORE this relic can run after it
guards.issue: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guard G8 owns this mechanism and verdicts it a gap; cited and matched under binding rule 3. C# enters a dedicated AutoPostPlay phase strictly BEFORE Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1160-1176), so every end-of-turn auto-play has already resolved -- and already left the hand -- when Cloak Clasp counts cards. The sim has no such phase: StampedePower fires from on_player_turn_end (powers.py:1025), the same walk this relic is in, so the answer depends on listener order. The seam's executed evidence is again this relic's: 'with a 5-card hand and Stampede 2, forcing Stampede first gives 3 block (the C# answer), the natural relics-before-powers order gives 5'. The ported Howl From Beyond card (cards/howl_from_beyond.py:45) is the same shape. Recorded separately from G1 because they are different missing structures -- G1 is sub-phase ordering WITHIN BeforeTurnEnd, G2 is a whole phase BEFORE it -- and fixing either alone leaves the other.

guards.rationale: The `player != base.Owner` / `card.Owner != base.Owner` / `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player (and, for the participants form, also admits pets). The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState) and models no pet creature, so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N2: the slot -- on_player_turn_end fires before the hand is discarded
guards.rationale: Load-bearing for a relic that counts the hand: BeforeSideTurnEnd precedes both EndOfTurnCleanup and FlushPlayerHand in C# (CombatManager.cs:1250-1255 and the flush that follows). The sim matches -- combat.py:654 fires on_player_turn_end, and only then come _process_turn_end_cards (:658) and `if self.hooks.should_flush_hand(): self.player.discard_hand()` (:662-663), with hooks.after_player_turn_end (the AfterTurnEnd slot, where relic/parrying_shield lives) after the flush. Confirmed by execution in `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order`, which shows on_player_turn_end as the last player-turn event before the next turn's on_block_cleared. Rule 7: combat.py is not hashed here.

The BlockVar is 1, so the multiply is the identity and the truncating cast can never bite; no AscensionHelper call in the file. C#'s `if (cards.Count != 0)` maps to the sim's `if player.hand`, and both are redundant against a 0-block application -- kept on both sides. Read carefully because a BlockVar of 1 is exactly the kind of constant a port drops as 'obviously 1' and then cannot ascend later.
The same list. Notably NOT the pile-limbo case of PROMPT.md bug class 7: this fires between plays, so no card is sitting in PileType.Play.

guards.what: N5: `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, num, ValueProp.Unpowered, null)` (CloakClasp.cs:33) vs `BlockCmd.apply(..., props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED)` (cloak_clasp.py:22-24)
guards.rationale: Same prop, and it matters: BlockCmd.apply skips modify_block_additive/multiplicative unless is_powered_attack(props) (cmds.py:141-144), so Dexterity does not add to Cloak Clasp's block. Same handling as relic/captains_wheel N3 in this batch. The card source is null on both sides.
